subject: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call summary (short):
- Use case: CloudHarbor will offer a new EU-facing analytics feature that will process end-customer data; customers are controllers.
- Deployment preference: Private deployment (VPC) option under evaluation.
- Compliance asks surfaced: DPA, SCC module choice, SOC 2 Type II report, subprocessors list, retention limits.

Redwood proposed path / asks from CloudHarbor:
1) DPA: we can start from Redwood's standard DPA and iterate. Please confirm any contractual clauses you must include (subprocessor notice windows, deletion/return timelines, audit windows).
2) SCC module: you mentioned a preference for a single-module approach — can you confirm which module (Module I/II/III) you prefer? On the call you said Module Two looked closest to your legal team's appetite.
3) Roles: please confirm whether CloudHarbor will be Controller and Redwood will act as Processor, or if you expect any joint-controller language for certain features.
4) Evidence: we can share a SOC 2 Type II summary and our current subprocessors list once you confirm the DPA path.

Next steps (proposed):
- I attach Redwood_SCC_Module_Matrix.xlsx and our standard DPA draft for your review. (attachment: Redwood_SCC_Module_Matrix.xlsx)
- If you confirm Module Two + Controller = CloudHarbor, I will loop Legal (Ben) to prepare an initial redline and send back a DPA.
- If you want any specific retention obligations or additional clauses, please flag those in reply or attach your procurement template.

Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up on Thursday 5/24 15:00 PT to go over the redline? If that works I’ll calendar an invite.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
(attachment: Redwood_SCC_Module_Matrix.xlsx)

From: Sara Mitchell <sara@cloudharbor.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check

Thanks Kim — great summary and yes, Thursday 5/24 15:00 PT works for us. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Roles: CloudHarbor will be the Controller for customer personal data. There are a couple of pipeline transforms where we act as controller-of-collection but for the Redwood integration we expect Redwood to be Processor.
- SCC module: our legal team prefers SCC Module Two for the vendor flow — it aligns best with our risk matrix.
- Contract items: we will need a DPA that includes: 30-day notice for subprocessor additions, ability to require removal of a subprocessor for cause, a 30–90 day data return/deletion window after contract termination, and a standard audit-rights clause.
- Evidence: please provide SOC 2 Type II report summary and current subprocessors list. I attached CloudHarbor_DPA_Request_20270522.pdf which is our procurement intake template — it captures the clauses above.

Procurement contact (cc’d for next steps): procurement@cloudharbor.com. Legal lead: Tim Owens (tim.owens@cloudharbor.com).

Appreciate it — Sara
Sara Mitchell
Head of Legal Ops
CloudHarbor
(attachment: CloudHarbor_DPA_Request_20270522.pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check

Ben / Lauren — forwarding CloudHarbor's reply. Key points: they confirm Controller = CloudHarbor, prefer SCC Module Two, and have an intake template attached requesting: 30-day subprocessor notice, right to remove subprocessor for cause, 30–90 day deletion window, and audit rights.

Can you advise on our recommended approach? My preference is to:
- Offer standard Redwood DPA + SCC Module Two (we have a Module Matrix attached)
- Provide SOC 2 Type II summary and subprocessors list up front
- Ask procurement to use our DPA draft for redlines (we’ll accept their template but prefer to start from ours).

Please confirm whether we need an exec escalation if their audit-rights wording is broader than our standard. Also can you prepare a short checklist of the minimal contract edits we will accept versus items that require Legal escalation?

>

Thanks,
Kim

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check

Kim / Lauren — thanks for the summary and forwarding Sara’s intake. Recommendation and immediate actions: 

1) Policy: proceed with Redwood's standard DPA and accept SCC Module Two as CloudHarbor requested. Module Two maps to the set of clauses they need and avoids the broader obligations in Module Three.
2) Subprocessors: we will accept the 30-day notice for new subprocessors and include a mutual discussion clause for removal for cause (we typically push for remediation first).
3) Deletion/Return window: Redwood standard is 60 days; we can accept a 30–90 day window but prefer to propose 60 days as a compromise.
4) Audit rights: we allow SOC 2 report review and a scoped on-site audit for cause; we will not agree to unlimited unfettered audit rights. We should propose a scoped process and provide our SOC 2 Type II summary instead of full report unless a DPIA-level review is required.

Deliverables (we will produce):
- Draft DPA with SCC Module Two pre-applied (I’ll attach the redline checklist and the proposed DPA draft). (attachment: SCC_redline_checklist.pdf)
- SOC 2 Type II summary and current subprocessors list (operations to attach SOC2_summary.pdf and subprocessors_list.csv).

I’ll prep the initial redline and circulate for internal sign-off today. Kimberly — please calendar the 5/24 15:00 PT touchpoint and include Legal + Procurement on the invite.

Ben Carter
Head of Contracts & Security Programs
Redwood Inference
(attachment: SCC_redline_checklist.pdf; request to ops for SOC2_summary.pdf)

From: Sara Mitchell <sara@cloudharbor.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudharbor.com, Tim Owens <tim.owens@cloudharbor.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudHarbor GDPR kickoff — DPA pathing & SCC module preference check

Thanks Ben / Kim — that sounds reasonable and aligned with our expectations. Confirming:
- We accept the draft workflow (start from Redwood DPA + SCC Module Two).
- 60-day deletion window is acceptable.
- We will review your SOC 2 summary first; if we require additional detail we will surface it at the 5/24 call.

Procurement will upload our procurement intake + any additional comments to the DocuSign link you provided. I’ve also attached a short procurement intake for our records.

We are on for the call now (5/24 15:00 PT). See you there.

Best,
Sara Mitchell
Head of Legal Ops
CloudHarbor
(attachment: CloudHarbor_DPA_Request_20270522.pdf)
